api/middleware.py — keeps unhandled server errors readable by the browser.

THE PROBLEM THIS EXISTS TO SOLVE
--------------------------------
Starlette builds the middleware stack as

    ServerErrorMiddleware -> [user middleware, e.g. CORSMiddleware] -> ExceptionMiddleware -> routes

`HTTPException`, `RequestValidationError` and every exception that has
its own `@app.exception_handler` (DatabaseUnavailable, AgentPoolSaturated,
AgentTaskTimeout in api/server.py) are answered by ExceptionMiddleware,
which sits INSIDE CORSMiddleware, so those responses get their
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header. An exception nobody handles (a
psycopg error, a plain bug) instead escapes all the way up to
ServerErrorMiddleware, the OUTERMOST layer, which writes its bare
"Internal Server Error" 500 from outside CORSMiddleware: no CORS
headers. The browser then refuses to expose that response to the page
and `fetch()` rejects with an opaque "TypeError: Failed to fetch" — so
every backend bug (e.g. the Build tab's move/rename hitting a database
permission error) looked like a connectivity problem, and the real
status code and message were invisible to the frontend.

(`@app.exception_handler(Exception)` does NOT help: Starlette routes
that one specifically to ServerErrorMiddleware too, so it has the same
problem.)

THE FIX
-------
UnhandledErrorMiddleware sits just INSIDE CORSMiddleware. It catches
whatever the routes/ExceptionMiddleware didn't handle and answers with a
JSON 500 in the same `{"de

api/routes/code_runs.py -- Patch S10: "grant more" for an M2C run that stopped at its credit ceiling.

    POST /v1/code/runs/{run_id}/grant        Authorization: Bearer <device JWT>        (no body)
         -> 200 {state: "running", run_credit_ceiling, run_credits_spent, granted_credits}

WHO CALLS IT. The device, with the same short-lived device JWT it gets from POST /v1/code/devices/token (S03). The
terminal shows the user "this run reached its credit limit; grant more?", and on a yes it calls this route. The web
app's session tokens are not accepted here: only a token whose type is `device` and whose device is live (the
verification, eo.devices.verify_device_token, checks both and that the device was not revoked).

WHAT A GRANT IS. A run in `paused_budget` goes back to `running` with a raised per-run ceiling (one chunk more than it
had already spent: codeagent/metering.py's RunCeilingPolicy decides how big a chunk is) and its turn is restarted. It
does NOT raise the account's pool: the pool is the account's plan, shared with the web app, and is only ever read here.
A grant while the pool is empty is refused (`quota_exhausted`, with the reset time) and changes nothing.

THE ORDER (every step before the claim only reads; every step after it is undone if it fails)

    2  the run is this account's AND this device's     404 run_not_found, the same body as a run that does not exi

api/routes/devices.py -- S03: the HTTP surface for M2C device pairing.

Two audiences, one router (mounted with a single include_router line in
api/server.py):

  The terminal (`m2c login`, no account session yet) -- /v1/code/devices/*
    POST /v1/code/devices/pair/start   {device_name, os, client_version}
         -> {device_code, user_code, verification_url, interval, expires_in}
    POST /v1/code/devices/pair/poll    {device_code}
         -> {status: pending | approved | denied | expired}; `approved` also
            carries {device_credential, device_id}, exactly once.
            An unknown or already-collected device_code is a 400.
    POST /v1/code/devices/token        {device_credential}
         -> {jwt, expires_in}   (a ~15 minute device JWT; 401 if the
            credential is unknown or the device was revoked)

  The signed-in web app (require_auth, the usual Supabase bearer) -- /api/devices*
    POST /api/devices/approve          {user_code} -> binds the terminal to the caller
    POST /api/devices/deny             {user_code} -> refuses it ("not my terminal")
    GET  /api/devices[?include_revoked=true]
                                       -> {devices: [...]}, the caller's own, active only by default
    POST /api/devices/{id}/revoke      -> {id, revoked_at}; 404 for anyone else's device

All the decisions live in eo/devices.py (read its docstring first); this
file only turns its outcomes into status codes. Status mapping:

    429  too many attempts: pair/

files.module_doc:
api/stream_tickets.py

Short-lived, single-use tickets for the two browser transports that can't
send an Authorization header: the /ws/{session_id} WebSocket and the
/api/task/{session_id}/stream EventSource (SSE).

Why this exists
---------------
Neither `new WebSocket(url)` nor `new EventSource(url)` lets the page set
request headers, so both used to carry the user's full Supabase access
token as `?token=<jwt>`. A query string is the one part of a request that
reliably ends up in places a header doesn't: uvicorn/proxy/CDN access
logs, Sentry breadcrumbs, browser history. A leaked access token is a
bearer credential for the *whole* API for as long as it lives (about an
hour), not just for the stream it was minted for.

How it works
------------
1. The page calls `POST /api/stream-ticket` (ordinary Authorization
   header, see api/routes/stream_ticket.py) saying which transport and
   which session_id it wants to open.
2. We mint a random ticket, store {user_id, kind, session_id} under the
   ticket's SHA-256 for TICKET_TTL_SECONDS, and hand the raw ticket back.
3. The page opens the socket/stream with `?ticket=<ticket>`.
4. The stream route redeems it with an atomic GETDEL: it is valid for one
   redemption only, even if two requests race, and expires on its own if
   nobody redeems it.

What a leaked ticket is worth: nothing after first use or ~30 seconds,
and it only ever opens the one transport/session it was minted for.

Design choices worth knowing
---------------------

api/task_runner.py

A programmatic sibling to eo/loop_v4.py's CLI dispatch. Reuses the same
underlying decision logic (imported straight from loop_v4, not
reimplemented) but returns structured dicts instead of printing to
stdout, so api/server.py can turn a task into a JSON response.

Tiers 0, 1, 2 run their full path here. Tier 3 has two branches: a
hires-driven path (_run_tier3_hires(), below) when the Panel actually
staffed the task, and a "not_wired_yet" placeholder for the no-hires
case — loop_v4.py's CLI-only tier-3 path blocks on input() for the
cost-ceiling confirmation and hands off to loop.py, a long-running
process that a single HTTP request/response cycle can't represent.

Deliberately does NOT modify loop_v4.py. It imports loop_v4's
underscore-prefixed helpers directly (_get_decision, in particular)
rather than duplicating the Inspector/panel/override logic — that logic
must never drift between the CLI and the API.

The same Starter General Agents pre-filter (eo/sga.py) that loop_v4.py's
CLI runs is used here too, so a task submitted through the API gets the
identical SGA-first treatment instead of always going straight to the
Inspector.

project_unique_name threads through run_task() -> _run_tier2() ->
execute_graph() -> file_manager.py, so a tier-2 task can target a
registered external project (eo/project_registry.py) instead of this
system's own apps/ directory. Only tier 2 touches disk, so tiers 0/1
don't need this parameter.
